newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed, nervous on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed, nervous on U.S. data.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Friday as Brady bonds retained some of their early gains while local bonds gave up gains as uncertainty resurfaced ahead of key U.S. inflation data in the coming week.
"Next week should be pretty complicated," said a trader at a foreign bank, pointing to the potential upsets from the release of U.S. producer price, consumer price and retail sales data.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 92-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was $0.12 lower at 115.03.

The market surged earlier in the day after statements by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan late Thursday in which he said the most likely path of the U.S. economy is of "moderate growth and low inflation."
The knee-jerk reaction of the market was to lower its fears that U.S. rates will not be hiked more than once more through the year.
But with next week's U.S. indicators the Federal Reserve could still be spooked by rising inflation so, the "rate outlook remains clouded," said another trader.
Call money fell to 5.83 percent from 5.98 percent.
